text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT 1719532468 — spike in 5xx/timeouts from scheduler-batcher in us-east-1. Error rate up 15% over baseline, tail latency climbing. Paging on-call. Metrics: https://grafana.redwood/inference/ops?panel=queue_depth

maya (oncall): I'm on pager. seeing a huge backlog on the serial-queue. batcher pods at 100% CPU and lots of inflight long sequences. any recent deploys?

rajesh: no deploys in last 2 hours. autoscaler shows no new nodes coming up — ASG at cap. could be head-of-line blocking from some large requests.

elaine: confirmed customer-facing errors: gateway returning 502/504 for a subset of requests. support is getting tickets. Zoe — can you estimate impacted customers?

zoe (support): initial triage: ~12 customers reporting increased latencies, 3 complaining failed requests. Some big customers on dedicated pools in us-east-1. I'll open a customer-impact doc.

maya (oncall): quick mitigation plan: (1) reduce batching window to force smaller batches, (2) enable overflow-route to fallback-model-lowmem, (3) evict long KV entries to free cache. Trying 1 now.

derek: reducing batching_window to 10ms on live config for the affected route. Patch applied: 
```json
{"route":"/v1/generate","batching_window_ms":10}
```

sre-bridge-bot: Config change deployed to 6/8 pods. Restarting remaining pods to pick up change.

rajesh: logs show a few requests with seq_length>12000 holding the KV cache and preventing other requests from progressing. Filtering them out might free the queue. Running a firewall rule to reject overly long sequences for now.

maya (oncall): can we evict the worst offenders from the queue? How do we identify?

elaine: use this query: 
```sql
SELECT request_id, seq_len, enqueue_ts FROM batch_queue WHERE state='queued' ORDER BY seq_len DESC LIMIT 20;
```
Got a handful with seq_len>15000. I'll mark them for preemptive-eviction.

derek: started eviction job, will drop the top 12 extreme seq requests and return 429 with friendly message. Command: 
```bash
/k8s/bin/evict-queue-entries --cluster=us-east-1 --ids=$(cat long_ids.txt)
```

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Eviction job completed. 12 requests evicted. Queue depth down 42%.

zoe (support): notifying affected customers with an explanation and mitigation steps. Triage doc: https://confluence.redwood/incidents/1719532468-impact

rajesh: after eviction and smaller batches, 5xx rate dropped to baseline in 90s. But we still see occasional 504s when the scheduler gets a burst.

maya (oncall): plan B — enable burst-capacity (temporary reserved slots) and route non-critical low-priority traffic to the cheaper fallback model until autoscaler capacity frees up. Rolling that now.

derek: burst-capacity toggled for us-east-1 pool + enabled fallback-route for routes: /embeddings, /async. Check: traffic draining to fallback.

elaine: monitoring customer error graphs — the three highest-impact customers are back to normal, remaining ones are degraded but improving. ETA to full recovery ~15-20m barring new spikes.

maya (oncall): handoff: I'm swapping with rajesh for extended mitigation and follow-up postmortem. @rajesh please own the post-eviction checks and the follow-up runbook.

rajesh: on it. I'll keep the channel updated and escalate to infra if ASG cap is still blocking scale. Need infra permission to bump cap.

sre-bridge-bot: Handoff recorded. New oncall: rajesh. Incident status: MITIGATED -> monitoring.

zoe (support): customers notified, one wants a callback. I'll coordinate with SE.

incident-bot: Summary: Actions taken: reduced batching_window, evicted oversized seq requests, enabled burst-capacity, routed low-priority traffic to fallback. Customer impact limited to ~12 customers, 3 had failed requests. Follow-ups: autoscaler ASG limit review, add guardrail on max sequence length upstream, improve alert to detect long-sequence head-of-line earlier.

maya (oncall): thanks team. Will create the postmortem draft with timestamps and action items.

rajesh: leaving notes here for PM/eng: consider per-request token caps and graceful degradation path to avoid KV starvation.

incident-bot: Thread closed for active work but left open for postmortem updates.
